title: Inference capacity plan
note: A replay of a recorded real session in three of its real turns: @builder’s turn that handed the app to @critic, @critic’s review, and @builder’s first turn after it that made a new version. Each says that turn’s words, shows the version it made, and reports its recorded cost. recordedTurns lists every real turn.
ask: @builder We serve an LLM inference API: about 40 requests a second at peak, bursty, and each request holds a GPU replica for 1.8 s on average. How many replicas do we need to keep the p99 wait under 500 ms, and what does each extra replica buy us? Give me a what-if I can drive: traffic, service time, burstiness and replicas, with live outcomes (p50 and p99 wait, utilization, cost per hour at $2.40 a replica-hour), and the curve that shows why waiting explodes near full utilization.

said: Layout looks right; tidying the tick labels, then handing it off for review.

**You need about 87 replicas.** At 40 req/s × 1.8 s, 72 replicas are busy on average. That's 83% utilization and $209 an hour, and it puts p99 wait at about 417 ms. The 87 depends on burstiness. I assumed an arrival CV² of 3 for "bursty" because you didn't give a number, so set it to what your traffic shows. With smooth (Poisson) traffic the count is lower.

**What each extra replica buys:** going from 73 to 74 replicas cuts p99 wait by 8.3 s. Near 87 one more replica saves only about 90 ms, for the same $2.40 an hour.

**In the app:**
- Drag **Peak traffic** or **Mean service time** in the left chart and watch the dot slide up the curve. Past about 90% utilization, wait goes from hundreds of milliseconds to tens of seconds.
- Raise **Burstiness** and the whole curve moves left, so you hit the wall at a lower utilization.
- In the right chart, click any dot to set the replica count. Dots that meet the target turn green; hover one to see its p99, its hourly cost and the wait it saves.

The numbers come from a standard queueing formula (Erlang C, with a correction for bursty traffic), not a simulation. "Wait" means time in the queue before a replica picks the request up, not generation time. I checked it in the light theme at 1280 px wide, but not yet in dark or at 375 px. The last update hasn't passed Postbox's check yet, and I didn't look at it after its final small fix to the axis labels.

@critic, please review the app.
I’ll inspect the app and its HTML, then pin concrete modeling and usability issues to the review.

Requested changes with four pinned comments: overlapping chart labels, overstated p99 certainty, inconsistent replica limits, and misleading chart boundaries. The app needs readable marginal-benefit details and clearer approximation limits before its capacity recommendation is dependable.

I fixed all ten problems Postbox's pre-display check found, so the app is now on v5. The capacity numbers haven't changed: 87 replicas at about $209 an hour.

- **Text size:** the charts now draw at the width they're shown at. Before, they were scaled down, which shrank the labels to 7–10 px; every label is now 12 px. At narrow widths the charts also show fewer ticks, so the axis labels no longer pile up.
- **Overlaps:** the caption above the left chart no longer runs into the chart. The right chart now labels only the first replica's saving and the selected one's, and its "first under target" note sits at the top, clear of the dots.
- **Other fixes:** each slider now has its own label. The dashed lines use 6 px dashes at 1.5 px wide. The app's own style classes have a prefix, so Postbox's styles no longer change them.

I looked at it again in the light theme at 1280 px wide and nothing overlaps. I haven't seen it in the dark theme or at 375 px, and the check on v5 hasn't reported back yet. The review request to critic is still open.
The safety check couldn't parse that heredoc, which held no removal. I'll put the edit script in a file and run that instead.

I've shipped v2 of the app as Postbox version 7, covering all four of critic's comments; they're answered and marked resolved on the review.

- **Replica chart:** the overlapping savings labels are gone. A detail row under the chart now shows the selected count's p99, its exact cost per hour, what the last replica saved and what one more would save.
- **Approximate numbers:** the headline and outcome strip now show "≈" and say "approx." A new service CV² slider (default 1) sets how much service times vary. A note under the strip says the p99 comes from a heuristic and should be checked against measured traffic or a simulation.
- **Replica slider:** its range now grows with traffic × service time, so the slider, the chart and the results always show the same count.
- **Utilization chart:** below 50% utilization the axis now extends down to your current point instead of saying "no queueing." Waits beyond 100 s get a ▲ marker with their value, instead of a flat line along the top.

I looked at the version before the last one in the light theme at 1280 px wide. The last change, shorter slider labels so all five fit on one line, hasn't been viewed, and its pre-display check is still pending.

app.title: GPU replicas vs. queueing delay
app.intent: Bursty 40 req/s at 1.8 s needs 87 replicas; waits explode near 100%.
app.code:
GPU replicas vs. queueing delay

Why waiting explodes: p99 wait vs. utilization

Fixed replica count; sweep traffic. Dot = you now. Faint curve = smooth (Poisson) traffic.

What each replica buys: p99 wait vs. replica count

Click a dot to set replicas. Labels: p99 saved by adding that replica.

Model: G/G/c queue, Erlang C with the Allen–Cunneen correction (wait × (CV²a+CV²s)/2), service CV² = 1, exponential tail for percentiles. Wait = time in queue before a replica picks the request up, not generation time. $2.40 per replica-hour.

review.title: GPU replicas vs. queueing delay
review.fallback: Review of GPU replicas vs. queueing delay: comment in the chat.

comments.text: The marginal-benefit labels overlap even in the wide render (−1.39 s and −840 ms), and SVG scaling shrinks them further on phones. Postbox also reports text below 12 px. Replace these floating labels with a readable selected-replica detail row showing p99, exact cost, and savings; keep chart text at least 12 rendered pixels at 375 px.

The headline presents 87 replicas as sufficient to hold p99 under 500 ms, but the implementation scales an Erlang C exponential tail using a mean-wait correction. That is a heuristic percentile estimate for bursty arrivals, not a validated G/G/c p99 guarantee. Mark the recommendation and p99 as approximate beside the numbers, expose the service-variability assumption there, and explain that measured traffic/service distributions or simulation are needed to validate the target.

Traffic and service sliders allow 120 req/s × 5 s = 600 busy replicas, while the replica slider stops at 300. The right chart then offers clickable counts above 600: clicking sets st.c above the slider maximum, leaving its thumb clamped at 300 while the label and results use a different value. Expand the replica range dynamically to cover the recommendation and chart, and keep every input value synchronized.

Below 50% utilization the chart says “no queueing,” although the model can still predict positive waiting probabilities and nonzero percentiles, particularly for small replica counts. Above 100 s it also silently clips the curve to the ceiling. Extend the utilization domain to include the current point and indicate values beyond the wait scale with an overflow marker and their numeric value, rather than substituting a false zero or flat ceiling.
